title: JavaScript Errors and Debugging: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on JavaScript error types, try/catch/finally, custom errors with error.cause, unhandled promise rejections, console methods, DevTools breakpoints and source maps.

chapters.title: Errors and Debugging Mental Model
points: An Error object carries name, message and stack; any value can be thrown, but throw Error objects so you get a stack trace

Built-in types: SyntaxError (fails at parse time, nothing runs), ReferenceError (undeclared variable), TypeError (wrong type or calling undefined, e.g. undefined.x), RangeError (value out of range, e.g. new Array(-1) or infinite recursion), URIError
Runtime errors bubble up the call stack until a catch handles them; if none does, the script or task dies and the error shows in the console
Async errors do not cross await-less boundaries: try/catch cannot catch a throw inside setTimeout or an un-awaited promise
Debugging loop: reproduce, read the message and stack top-down, isolate with a breakpoint or log, fix, re-test

chapters.title: try/catch/finally and Throwing Errors
points: try { risky() } catch (err) { handle(err) } finally { cleanup() } - finally runs on success, on throw and even after return
Optional catch binding: catch { ... } when the error object is not needed
A return inside finally overrides the try or catch return value and swallows any pending throw
throw new Error('msg') creates a stack at the throw site; throw 'string' has no stack and breaks instanceof checks
Rethrow what you cannot handle: if (!(err instanceof ValidationError)) throw err; never leave an empty catch
catch only sees synchronous throws and awaited rejections: try { await fetch(url) } catch(e) {} works, but fetch(url) without await escapes it

chapters.title: Custom Errors and error.cause
points: class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(msg, opts) { super(msg, opts); this.name = 'ValidationError'; } } - call super first and set name
Check type with err instanceof ValidationError instead of matching message strings
Wrap lower-level failures: throw new Error('Load failed', { cause: err }) keeps the original error attached as err.cause
Walk the chain with a loop over err.cause; DevTools and Node print the nested cause under the main stack
Add extra context as fields (this.field = 'email', this.status = 404) so handlers can branch without parsing messages

chapters.title: Unhandled Promise Rejections
points: A rejected promise with no .catch or await in try/catch fires the unhandledrejection event (window.addEventListener in browsers) or process.on('unhandledRejection') in Node
Node 15+ terminates the process on an unhandled rejection by default; browsers only log it
An async function always returns a promise, so a throw inside it becomes a rejection, never a synchronous throw
Forgetting await or return in a promise chain detaches it, so its error is never caught by the outer try/catch
Promise.all rejects on the first failure and ignores the rest; Promise.allSettled returns {status, value|reason} for every promise
Use a global unhandledrejection handler only for logging and reporting, not as the normal error path

chapters.title: Console Methods, Breakpoints and DevTools
points: console.log/info/warn/error for severity levels; console.error and warn show stack traces and filter separately in DevTools
console.table(arrayOfObjects) prints a grid; console.dir(obj) shows the object tree; console.group/groupEnd indent related logs
console.time('t') then console.timeEnd('t') measures elapsed time; console.assert(cond, msg) logs only when cond is false; console.trace() prints the call stack

Breakpoint kinds: line-of-code, conditional (pause only when an expression is true), logpoint (logs without editing code), DOM change, XHR/fetch, event listener, exception (pause on caught or uncaught)
The debugger; statement pauses execution when DevTools is open, like a hard-coded breakpoint
While paused: Step over (F10), Step into (F11), Step out (Shift+F11), Resume (F8); inspect Scope, Call Stack and Watch expressions

chapters.title: Source Maps and Debugging Cheat Sheet
points: A source map (.map file) links minified or transpiled output back to original source so stack traces and breakpoints show your real files and lines
Enabled via a //# sourceMappingURL=app.js.map comment at the end of the bundle; build tools emit them with sourcemap: true (or devtool setting in webpack)
Production: ship maps privately (upload to Sentry or similar, or hidden source maps) to avoid exposing source code, and keep the map version matched to the deployed build
Node: run with node --enable-source-maps, and node --inspect (or --inspect-brk) to attach Chrome DevTools

Cheat sheet: Error types TypeError/ReferenceError/RangeError/SyntaxError; finally always runs; new Error(msg, {cause}); instanceof for custom errors; await inside try; unhandledrejection listener; console.table/time/trace; debugger; F8/F10/F11
